setup: Stand tall on a low plyo box or aerobic step (typically 15 to 30 cm high) near the front edge.
Fix your gaze straight ahead and brace your core.
steps: Step off the edge with one foot without jumping upward or pushing off aggressively.
Drop straight down and contact the floor with the balls of your landing foot first, immediately rolling to the heel.
Absorb the impact softly by flexing simultaneously at your ankle, knee, and hip into a balanced athletic quarter-squat.
Freeze upon landing and hold the single-leg stance motionless briefly.
Step back up onto the box and reset before the next repetition.
instructions.breathing: Exhale sharply as your foot contacts the ground to brace your trunk, holding steady through the pause.

common_faults.fault: Landing with a stiff, locked knee and loud impact.
common_faults.correction: Actively yield into ankle dorsiflexion, knee flexion, and hip flexion to decelerate silently.

common_faults.fault: Knee caving inward (valgus collapse) on contact.
common_faults.correction: Engage the hip abductors and keep your kneecap tracking directly over your second and third toes.

common_faults.fault: Jumping upward off the box instead of stepping off.
common_faults.correction: Step directly forward or downward so gravity drives the drop without adding extra vertical momentum.

precautions: Begin on a low surface (15 cm) to verify joint tolerance and control before progressing box height.

name: Single-Leg Drop Landing
summary: A unilateral landing drill where you step off a low box and absorb force quietly on one leg, holding the position to develop deceleration control and stability.
